title: DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Each worker objective fᵢ is differentiable and convex on ℝᵈ, with an Lᵢ-Lipschitz gradient. The average objective is therefore convex.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective is F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x) for n ≥ 1 workers. Their common minimizer set X = ⋂ᵢ argmin fᵢ is nonempty and equals argmin F.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A completed query at worker i returns gᵢ(x,ξ), a jointly measurable estimate with mean ∇fᵢ(x). Each worker consumes its own IID sample stream in completion order. Streams are independent across workers and their laws νᵢ may differ.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, system and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID; LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient; LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: The timed oracle has a central node and n computing leaves. Each leaf can have one gradient query pending, takes hᵢ > 0 per completed query, and supports cancellation. Each directed star link can carry one message at a time. Distinct links and worker computations can operate concurrently. A k-bit payload costs l + b(k + 64) time, including the clock overhead, with l,b ≥ 0.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, system, spec.numWorkers and spec.valid; LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, computation and communication; LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits and step

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every worker i and query point x, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ) − ∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σ² with σ ≥ 0. This uniform bound permits positive variance at a common minimizer.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, spec.valid and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.variance_integrable and IsStochasticGradient.variance

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, F(x) − min F ≥ (μ/2) dist(x,X)², with μ > 0 and nμ ≤ ∑ᵢ Lᵢ. The growth condition applies to the average objective and allows multiple common minimizers.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries, gradient replies and the output lie in Euclidean ℝᵈ, with d a public natural number.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, Params.d, Point, spec.ComputeQuery, spec.ComputeReply and spec.Output

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Weak interpolation holds at the level of worker objectives. Some z minimizes every fᵢ and satisfies ‖x₀ − z‖ ≤ R, while individual minimizer sets may be larger than their intersection. All Params fields are public, including x₀, R ≥ 0, ε > 0, σ, μ, each Lᵢ ≥ 0, and the network timings. The functions, common minimizer, gradient mappings and sampling laws are instance or oracle data.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, Params, solutions, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.valid and spec.admissible

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: The output is a single point read from the algorithm's designated root at the prescribed elapsed-time deadline. Its error is the squared Euclidean distance to the common minimizer set X.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, solutions, spec.Output and spec.successful; LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable, its squared distance to X integrable, and E[dist(output,X)²] ≤ ε under the joint algorithm and oracle law. Execution must also have finitely many events almost surely through the deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedWeakInterpolation.lean, spec.successful; LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents and TimedConvergence

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines shared minimizers and quadratic growth of the average with noisy worker gradients, heterogeneous computation times, and concurrent star links that charge latency and time per bit. It evaluates expected squared distance to the common solution set at a fixed elapsed-time deadline.

descriptionHtml:
Distributed Minimization under Weak Interpolation

We minimize the average of smooth convex worker objectives on the Euclidean space Rd of dimension d≥0. Their common minimizer set S is nonempty, the given starting point lies within a known radius of S, and the average satisfies quadratic growth relative to S. Workers communicate through a hub and return unbiased local stochastic gradients with bounded variance, using independent samples within and across workers. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯ whose expected squared Euclidean distance to S is at most ε by the elapsed-time deadline.

Let n≥1 be the number of workers, with local objectives fi:Rd→R for i=1,…,n. Write F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x). The optimization problem is minx∈RdF(x). The algorithm receives d, n, the measurable sample space Ω, the worker computation times hi>0, the latency ℓ≥0, the time per bit b≥0, the smoothness constants Li≥0, the growth constant μ>0, the radius R≥0, the noise bound σ≥0, the tolerance ε, and the starting point x0∈Rd. The parameters satisfy nμ≤∑i=1nLi.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Local convexity and smoothness). Each fi is convex and differentiable on Rd, with ∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤Li∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd.

Assumption 2 (Common minimizers and quadratic growth). Let S=⋂i=1nargminx∈Rdfi(x) and write dist(x,S)=infz∈S∥x−z∥. There exists x⋆∈S such that ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,F(x)−F(x⋆)≥μ2dist(x,S)2for all x∈Rd.

Assumption 3 (Local stochastic gradients). Worker i has a sequence (ξi,k)k≥0 of measurable i.i.d. samples with law νi on Ω. The worker sequences are mutually independent, and the entire sample array is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. At any query point x∈Rd, the worker returns x and gi(x,ξi,k), where k counts its previously completed evaluations. The map gi:Rd×Ω→Rd is jointly measurable. For each x and ξ∼νi, the vector gi(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and its squared error is integrable, with Eξ∼νi[gi(x,ξ)]=∇fi(x),Eξ∼νi[∥gi(x,ξ)−∇fi(x)∥2]≤σ2.

The star network consists of the n computing workers and one communication hub. An evaluation at worker i takes time hi. Each worker can have one evaluation in progress and may abort it without consuming a sample. An evaluation request made while the worker is busy is ignored. Messages travel only between the hub and a worker. A payload of m bits is transmitted with 64 appended zero bits and takes time ℓ+b(m+64). The recipient receives the sender’s identity and the transmitted bits. Each directed link carries at most one message at a time and ignores submissions while occupied. Distinct directed links, including opposite directions of the same connection, can operate concurrently with one another and with worker computations.

For an elapsed-time budget T≥0, almost surely the algorithm must process finitely many events at every deadline t∈[0,T]. At time T, its designated output node must produce a measurable point x¯∈Rd with integrable squared distance to S satisfying E[dist(x¯,S)2]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness and the worker sample array.

On Rd, the n convex, Li-smooth worker objectives have a common minimizer set S=⋂iarg⁡minfi≠∅. Their average f satisfies f(x)−minf≥μdist(x,S)2/2, with 0<nμ≤∑iLi and dist(x0,S)≤R. On the coordinator star, one gradient at worker i takes hi>0 seconds and a k-bit message takes ℓ+bk seconds. import LongTails.Setups.DistributedSmoothNonconvex
import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.HausdorffDistance

open MeasureTheory DistributedTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.DistributedWeakInterpolation

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  n : ℕ+
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  h : Fin n → Time
  l : Time
  b : Time
  L : Fin n → ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
abbrev Functions (p : Params) := Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ
abbrev Samples (p : Params) := Fin p.n → ℕ → p.Ω

def solutions (p : Params) (f : Functions p) : Set (Point p) :=
  {x | ∀ i, IsMinOn (f i) Set.univ x}

noncomputable def objective (p : Params) (f : Functions p) (x : Point p) : ℝ :=
  (∑ i, f i x) / p.n

noncomputable def system (p : Params) (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)) :=
  StarNetwork.system ⟨p.h, p.l, p.b⟩ (fun i x (s : Samples p) k => g i x (s i k)) P

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n + 1
  Instance := Functions
  ComputeQuery p := StarNetwork.ComputeQuery (Point p)
  ComputeReply p := StarNetwork.ComputeReply (Point p) (Point p)
  CommReply p := StarNetwork.CommReply p.n
  Output := Point
  publicInput := id
  valid p := (∀ i, 0 < p.h i) ∧ (∀ i, 0 ≤ p.L i) ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧
    p.n * p.μ ≤ ∑ i, p.L i ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (f i) ∧ (∀ x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
      ∀ x y, ‖gradient (f i) x - gradient (f i) y‖ ≤ p.L i * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ z ∈ solutions p f, ‖p.x0 - z‖ ≤ p.R ∧ ∀ x,
      p.μ / 2 * Metric.infDist x (solutions p f) ^ 2 ≤ objective p f x - objective p f z) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) (ν : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)), O = system p g P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (s : Samples p) => s i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (s : Samples p) => s i k)
        (ν i : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
        StochasticSmoothAndConvex.IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (ν i) (f i) (g i) p.σ
  successful p f output P := Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun s => Metric.infDist (output s) (solutions p f) ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
    ∫ s, Metric.infDist (output s) (solutions p f) ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.DistributedWeakInterpolation
